stage_name: solver round 1 passed; leak read round 3 running, then the judge
stump: A competent solver stages the book, reads the model team's cumulative default curve from month 1 for every loan's next 12 months or remaining term and books about 44 per cent too much (about AUD 19.8 million against AUD 13,773,000); the step that lands it there is treating a curve that runs from origination as a term structure from the reporting date, when most of the book is past its riskiest months.

leak.leak_py: REVIEW, no LEAK (six lines: model-team wording, call vocabulary, stump-term counts, post-reporting dates), after the round 2 repair
leak.reader: round 1: no decisive-step sentence, no ranking or answer file, no planted file; realism defects on the calculation path (DPD off the repayment calendar, balances on the annuity to the cent with eight round-hundred tuning edits, hardship arrangements before funding, curve defaults in months 1-3, stage 3 count open at 180+ DPD) taken into a realism rebuild; round 2: twelve findings fixed in the generator (allowance now AUD 13,773,000), next read pending

solver_rounds.brief: Both solvers read the curve from each loan's months on book (the decisive starting-point rung) and stopped at the unconditional increment, the -3.3% rung; both named the survival-conditioned reading (A$13,773k) and declined it because CRM-ECL-04 does not spell it out. Read as a stump, not a fork: 3.2 defines PD(k) as the probability of default in the k-th month after the reporting date for a loan performing on that date, and the curve is the probability that a new loan defaults by each month on book. The judge rules on it at stage 7.
